rationales.LC: In the default simulated configuration the jailbreak handler succeeds only if the agent declares a jailbreak vulnerability, and CodeBot declares capability abuse and prompt injection only, so roleplay text does not reach a tool call or guardrail-bypass sink. The prompt that tells the model to go along with roleplay is LLM mode, which is not the default.
rationales.CP: Memory carryover is limited to MemoryBot's in-process list; other chat agents, including CodeBot, answer only the latest user turn and do not store attacker context.
rationales.AP: The assessed path ends in a CodeBot chat reply on the same component. Orchestrator-to-Worker delegation is declared but not implemented, and this path does not call another agent.
rationales.RH: The packet describes no evaluator, verifier, or reward channel on the CodeBot roleplay path, and it records neither an isolation test nor a verified reward-hacking episode.
rationales.ES: CodeBot lists shell and file tools, but chat-agent tool names are not executed except on separate scripted paths, and LLM mode passes no tools to the model, so no dynamic extension is reachable here.

score.automatable_rationale: The in-repo solution is three documented prompts, and static reading indicates none reaches a success reply under the default simulated handler, so there is no repeatable unattended exploit against the scored configuration.
score.technical_impact_rationale: Default mode does not enter unrestricted mode or invoke tools. Even the documented sink is only a chat reply, and CodeBot's shell and file tools are persona declarations rather than executed bindings, so impact is not total control.

applicability_as_implemented.rationale: Default startup is simulated mode: generateResponseImpl does not call a model, and CodeBot returns regex-scripted text without selecting or sequencing tool actions.

applicability_as_modeled.rationale: The lab models CodeBot as a persona and, in optional LLM mode, as one chat completion whose prompt goes along with roleplay. No tools are passed, so the model returns text only and does not pursue goals or sequence actions.
